theory.intro: The PAYG instalments withheld from each pay are only an estimate of the tax that will be owed. At the end of the financial year a tax return compares the **total instalments** already withheld with the **total tax payable**. Withhold too much and the ATO pays the difference back as a **tax refund**; withhold too little and there is a **tax liability** — an amount still owing.
facts: $\text{Refund or amount owing}=\text{Total instalments}-\text{Total tax payable}$
A positive result is a refund; a negative result is an amount owing, and its size is the size of that negative number.
When the two totals are equal there is neither a refund nor an amount owing.
$\text{Total tax payable}=\text{Income tax payable}+\text{Medicare levy}$, so the levy must be included before the comparison is made.
$\text{Total instalments}=\text{Instalment per pay period}\times\text{Number of pay periods}$, using $52$ weeks, $26$ fortnights or $12$ months in a year.
steps: Subtract the total tax payable from the total instalments

foundation.question_text:
A delivery driver has a tax payable of $\$9480$ and his PAYG instalments for the year totalled $\$10\,725$.
Determine his tax refund or amount owing, to the nearest cent.
foundation.solution_text:
$\text{Total instalments}-\text{Total tax payable}=10\,725-9480$
$=1245$
The balance is positive, so he receives a tax refund of $\$1245.00$.

$=-1380$

foundation.question_text:
A seasonal grape picker has a tax payable of $\$5318$ and his PAYG instalments for the year totalled $\$4975$.
Does he receive a tax refund or does he have an amount owing? Justify your answer.
foundation.solution_text:
Compare the two totals.
$4975<5318$
The instalments withheld are less than the tax payable, so he has not paid enough tax and has an amount owing.

foundation.question_text:
A truck driver has PAYG instalments of $\$318.50$ withheld each week for $52$ weeks, and his tax payable is $\$15\,940$.
Determine his tax refund or amount owing, to the nearest cent.
foundation.solution_text:
1. **Find the total instalments paid**
$\text{Total instalments}=318.50\times52$
$=\$16\,562$
2. **Subtract the total tax payable from the total instalments**
$16\,562-15\,940=622$
The balance is positive, so he receives a tax refund of $\$622.00$.

development.question_text:
A parcel courier's tax payable is $\$13\,338$ and she is paid fortnightly.
Calculate the equal fortnightly PAYG instalment that would have left her with neither a refund nor an amount owing, to the nearest cent.
development.solution_text:
For a nil balance the total instalments must equal the tax payable.
$\text{Instalment}=13\,338\div26$
$=\$513.00$

development.question_text:
A courier expected a tax refund of $\$820$. He then found a receipt for a further allowable deduction, which reduced his tax payable by $\$364$.
Calculate his new tax refund, to the nearest cent.
development.solution_text:
The instalments are unchanged, so a smaller tax payable makes the refund larger by the same amount.
$\text{New refund}=820+364$
$=\$1184.00$

mastery.question_text:
A parcel courier has a taxable income of $\$67\,400$ and had PAYG instalments of $\$425$ withheld each fortnight for $26$ fortnights.
$\begin{array}{l|l} \textbf{Taxable income} & \textbf{Tax on this income} \\ \hline \$0\text{ to }\$18\,200 & \text{Nil} \\ \$18\,201\text{ to }\$45\,000 & 19\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$18\,200 \\ \$45\,001\text{ to }\$120\,000 & \$5092\text{ plus }32.5\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$45\,000 \\ \$120\,001\text{ to }\$180\,000 & \$29\,467\text{ plus }37\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$120\,000 \\ \$180\,001\text{ and over} & \$51\,667\text{ plus }45\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$180\,000 \end{array}$
Use the tax table to determine his tax refund or amount owing, to the nearest cent. Ignore the Medicare levy.
mastery.solution_text:
1. **Find the total tax payable**
$\text{Total tax payable}=5092+0.325\times(67\,400-45\,000)$
$=5092+0.325\times22\,400$
$=\$12\,372$
2. **Find the total instalments paid**
$\text{Total instalments}=425\times26$
$=\$11\,050$
3. **Subtract the total tax payable from the total instalments**
$11\,050-12\,372=-1322$
The balance is negative, so he has an amount owing of $\$1322.00$.

mastery.question_text:
A farm worker received a tax refund of $\$1148$ after $\$210$ was withheld from each of his $52$ weekly pays.
$\begin{array}{l|l} \textbf{Taxable income} & \textbf{Tax on this income} \\ \hline \$0\text{ to }\$18\,200 & \text{Nil} \\ \$18\,201\text{ to }\$45\,000 & 19\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$18\,200 \\ \$45\,001\text{ to }\$120\,000 & \$5092\text{ plus }32.5\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$45\,000 \\ \$120\,001\text{ to }\$180\,000 & \$29\,467\text{ plus }37\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$120\,000 \\ \$180\,001\text{ and over} & \$51\,667\text{ plus }45\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$180\,000 \end{array}$
Use the tax table to calculate his taxable income, to the nearest dollar. Ignore the Medicare levy.
mastery.solution_text:
$\text{Total instalments}=210\times52$
$=\$10\,920$
$\text{Total tax payable}=10\,920-1148$
$=\$9772$
The tax is more than $\$5092$ but less than $\$29\,467$, so the taxable income lies in the third bracket.
$0.325\times\text{Excess}=9772-5092$
$=4680$
$\text{Excess}=4680\div0.325$
$=\$14\,400$
$\text{Taxable income}=45\,000+14\,400$
$=\$59\,400$

mastery.question_text:
Two couriers each have a tax payable of $\$14\,872$. Anh had $\$560$ withheld each fortnight for $26$ fortnights, while Bede had $\$1290$ withheld each month for $12$ months.
Determine each courier’s tax refund or amount owing, to the nearest cent.
mastery.solution_text:
$\text{Anh's instalments}=560\times26$
$=\$14\,560$
$14\,560-14\,872=-312$
Anh has an amount owing of $\$312.00$.
$\text{Bede's instalments}=1290\times12$
$=\$15\,480$
$15\,480-14\,872=608$
Bede receives a tax refund of $\$608.00$.
